data.title: Lenovo Group: Q2 Financial Results 2026/27
data.description:
Lenovo Group: Q2 Financial Results 2026/27

Lenovo delivers record Q2 performance, confident in long-term Hybrid AI opportunities

Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY), together with its subsidiaries (‘the Group’), today reported second quarter results for fiscal year 2026/27, demonstrating strong growth, a leap forward in profitability, and structural enhancements to the Group’s business fundamentals.

Overall Group revenue for the second quarter reached an all-time high of US$30.2 billion, up 48% year-on-year. All business groups delivered record second-fiscal-quarter revenue while demonstrating strong profitability, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) becoming an engine of hyper-growth with operating profit surpassing US$1 billion for the first time. Adjusted net income[1] was up 166% year-on-year to US$1.4 billion, with adjusted net margin improvements of two percentage points year-on-year. AI-related revenue[2] grew 79% year-on-year, surpassing the US$10 billion mark for the first time and accounting for 36% of total Group revenue in Q2.

Performance was underpinned by broad-based momentum across the Group’s diversified portfolio and balanced growth across all sales geographies. Business fundamentals continued to strengthen as faster growth in higher-value segments reshaped the Group’s profit mix. This diversification helps mitigate industry-wide cost pressures and exposure to device-demand cycles, supporting a more resilient and sustainable profitability profile.

The Group continues to maintain disciplined cash and capital management, balancing strong revenue growth and industry-wide higher component costs with controlled capital expenditure and credit risk controls for large AI infrastructure projects. In this quarter, it generated US$1.6 billion in operating cash flow and US$1.2 billion in free cash flow.

Market Outlook

Lenovo remains highly confident in the long-term growth opportunities across both infrastructure and devices. As AI shifts from training to inferencing, rapidly expanding real-world use cases are driving sustained compute demand across cloud, edge, and enterprise environments. Cloud Service Provider revenue for the Group grew nearly 170% year-on-year, and Enterprise & SMB infrastructure revenue was up 200% year-on-year. At the same time, AI democratization is creating new demand for intelligent, agent-enabled devices as well as new form factors, as more AI data and workloads are generated at the edge. With a full-stack Hybrid AI portfolio spanning devices, edge, infrastructure, solutions and services, Lenovo is uniquely positioned as a full-stack player to capture opportunities and value across the market, as well as extend its leadership.

Lenovo’s Board of Directors declared an interim dividend of 9.0 HK cents per share.

Chairman and CEO quote – Yuanqing Yang:

“Lenovo delivered another exceptional quarter, where we have sustained strong growth, made a leap forward in profitability, and structurally enhanced our business fundamentals, together demonstrating the success of our transformation from a PC leader into a global full-stack compute leader. Now, the real-world AI adoption is booming, which will not only drive sustained growth in infrastructure demand but also unlock tremendous growth potential in the device market. With our Hybrid AI strategy, full-stack portfolio across Client-Edge-Cloud, as well as strong financial discipline and operational resilience, we are confident in sustaining this strong momentum and reaching US$100 billion in annual revenue as early as this fiscal year.”

CFO quote – Winston Cheng:

“Our results this quarter demonstrate the strength of Lenovo’s geographically diverse business and balanced customer mix, while marking further progress toward our long-term net-margin ambitions of more than 5%. This, combined with disciplined working-capital management and controlled capital expenditure, gives us the flexibility to invest in organic growth while maintaining strong liquidity, a resilient balance sheet and our investment-grade credit profile. Together, our operational excellence and financial discipline position Lenovo to capture long-term demand for AI compute and deliver sustainable, profitable growth.”

Q2 results:

Intelligent Devices Group (IDG):

  • Revenue for IDG increased 15% year-on-year to record second fiscal quarter revenue of US$17.4 billion, with double-digit year-on-year revenue growth from PCs and smart devices.
  • IDG’s industry-leading operating margin was well maintained at 7.1%, despite a challenging market environment, reflecting the Group’s operational excellence, supply chain resilience, and continued innovation.
  • Global PC market share leadership was further strengthened, reaching 23.8% and extending Lenovo’s lead over the #2 player to an all-time high of more than seven percentage points.
  • The smartphone business delivered record second-quarter revenue, with double-digit year-on-year growth.

Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG):

  • ISG delivered the strongest quarter in its history in terms of both revenue and profit, with revenue reaching US$11.3 billion, up 178% year-on-year, and operating profit exceeding US$1 billion for the first time. Operating margin expanded to a record 9.6%.
  • ISG strengthened its global market leadership in traditional server, ranking number one in global x86 server shipments for the first time with 16%[3] market share, up six percentage points year-on-year.
  • Enterprise & SMB revenue grew 200% year-on-year. GPU server revenue grew more than 300% year-on-year, supported by a pipeline that grew 48% quarter-on-quarter to US$80 billion.
  • In the first full quarter as part of the Lenovo Group, Infinidat delivered its best quarter ever – with the high-end storage portfolio expanding ISG’s enterprise storage capabilities.

Solutions and Services Group (SSG):

  • SSG delivered record quarterly revenue of US$3.1 billion, up 20% year-on-year, and surpassing US$3 billion for the first time. Operating margin expanded 3.7 percentage points to a record 26%.
  • SSG is growing nearly 2x faster than the broader services market, an outperformance increasingly being driven by higher-value segments as enterprise AI-led offerings accelerate. Managed Services, Projects & Solutions reached a record 63% of SSG revenue, demonstrating the strength of SSG’s tech-led, labor-light model.
  • AI Services continued to deliver triple-digit year-on-year revenue growth, as SSG scaled repeatable AI-powered solutions and Lenovo IP across industries, with momentum in areas including retail, manufacturing and sports.
  • AI Library is also scaling proven, validated use cases across industries and functions, helping customers move from AI experimentation to measurable business outcomes up to 24 times faster.

Corporate highlights

Achievements, announcements, and notable commitments over the past quarter include:

  • Lenovo climbed 43 places to #153 on Fortune’s annual Global 500 List, making it the highest ranking in the company’s history and one of the most significant advances in recent years. The recognition underscores Lenovo’s position as one of the world’s 500 largest companies by revenue.
  • Lenovo received the highest possible rating by Hang Seng Indexes company advancing from its AA+ rating of last year to AAA this year, as well as the highest Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) scores for any company within the technology industry.
  • The Group was named to TIME’s World’s Best Companies 2026 list for the first time, ranking no. 51 globally among leading companies worldwide. The ranking, developed by TIME in partnership with Statista, recognizes top-performing companies around the world based on three primary dimensions: employee satisfaction, revenue growth, and sustainability transparency. Lenovo achieved an overall score of 87.51, with its growth performance categorized as “Very High.”
  • For the third year in a row, Fast Company recognized Lenovo among its annual Best Workplaces for Innovators list. The Group was named as a finalist in both the Best Workplaces for Innovators: AI, Automation and Machine Learning Excellence and Best Workplaces for Innovators: North America categories.
  • Lenovo has been recognized as a World’s Top Disability Inclusive business through the Disability Index, the world’s leading benchmarking tool for measuring and advancing disability inclusion in business.
  • Tech World, Lenovo’s annual global innovation event, will return to CES® 2027 in Las Vegas. Hosted at Sphere and part of the CES Keynote lineup, Tech World will bring together a visionary lineup of speakers and breakthrough innovations with a first-of-its-kind immersive technology and music experience.

[1] Note on adjusted net income: Adjusted measure was defined as financial metric by excluding net fair value changes on financial assets at fair value through profit or loss, amortization of intangible assets resulting from mergers and acquisitions, impairment and write-off of intangible assets and property, plant and equipment, fair value change on derivative financial liabilities relating to warrants, notional interest on convertible bonds, and dilution gain on interest in an associate; and the corresponding income tax effects, if any.

[2] Note on AI-related revenue: AI Devices: PCs and Smartphones equipped with NPU; AI Servers: GPU Servers; AI Services: Services that enable customer to build, scale & manage AI.

[3] x86 server market share is calculated after excluding ODM Direct x86 server units from total x86 server market units.

About Lenovo

Lenovo is a US$83 billion revenue global technology powerhouse, ranked #153 in the Fortune Global 500, and serving millions of customers every day in 180 markets. Guided by its vision of “Smarter Technology for All”, Lenovo is executing a Hybrid AI strategy that spans Personal AI – one personal AI, multiple devices; and Enterprise AI – helping customers turn data into insights and value. This strategy is delivered through the Group’s commitment to world-class innovation and a full-stack AI portfolio, including devices (PCs, workstations, smartphones, tablets, accessories), infrastructure solutions (server, storage, edge, high-performance computing and software defined infrastructure), as well as software, solutions, and services. With a global footprint spanning more than 20 research and development locations and a global supply chain that includes more than 30 manufacturing sites across 11 markets, Lenovo is widely recognized for its operational excellence. Lenovo is listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange under Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY). Learn more at www.lenovo.com and follow the latest news in our newsroom.

data.title: BOJ's Ueda Vows to Keep Careful Eye on Fed Moves — Update
data.description:
By Megumi Fujikawa

TOKYO--Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda pledged to closely watch how Federal Reserve policy changes affect growth and inflation in Japan, while reaffirming his readiness to keep tightening monetary settings.

"With the Fed raising interest rates and many other central banks pivoting toward hikes, we need to carefully monitor how those rate moves and the accompanying changes in global financial conditions affect Japan's economy and prices," Ueda told a parliamentary committee on Thursday.

Ueda noted that currency fluctuations--which can be heavily swayed by Fed policy--are more likely to affect domestic prices than in the past as companies in Japan become more comfortable passing on costs to consumers.

"We will conduct monetary policy appropriately while keeping in mind that these shifts could in turn influence underlying inflation through changes in inflation expectations," he added.

While BOJ policymakers are cautious about cooling the economy with monetary tightening, further action looks necessary to keep inflation in check, especially as heightened expectations for Fed rate hikes pressure the yen.

Market participants see a growing chance that the BOJ could raise rates again as soon as December. The Fed is also widely expected to hike next month as U.S. inflation continues to concern officials.

The BOJ is keeping an eye on inflation too. Ueda again stressed the importance of anchoring underlying consumer inflation around 2% so it doesn't overshoot the central bank's target and hurt the economy.

He warned that one measure of underlying inflation--consumer prices excluding fresh food--is likely to accelerate clearly above 2% as firms pass on higher labor costs, oil remains expensive and yen weakness persists. Surging global demand related to the artificial-intelligence buildout adds another inflationary impulse.

In September, that gauge of underlying inflation accelerated to 2.1% year-on-year from August's 1.7%. Economists polled by data provider Quick expect October figures due Friday to show a further rise to 2.3%.

The BOJ said last month that underlying inflation had reached its 2% target for the first time since the goal was introduced in 2013. It held policy settings steady at its previous meeting in October after raising rates to 1.25% in September.

Despite the rate hikes delivered so far, the BOJ governor still sees Japan's financial conditions as accommodative, although he acknowledged that monetary tightening is affecting households and businesses through higher mortgage rates and funding costs.

"The bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation, in response to developments in economic activity and prices as well as financial conditions," he said.

Write to Megumi Fujikawa at megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com

(END) Dow Jones Newswires

data.title: LGS Lab Gas System Launches Next Generation Ultra High Purity Laboratory Gas Delivery System Solutions
data.description:
SHANGHAI, CN / ACCESS Newswire / November 18, 2026 / LGS Lab Gas System, a leading manufacturer and engineering contractor of ultra high purity gas delivery equipment, today announced its expanded suite of centralized laboratory gas supply systems and precision fluid handling components. Designed to meet the rigorous demands of semiconductor fabrication, pharmaceutical development, biotechnology, and analytical testing, the integrated product line ensures stable pressure control and parts per billion purity from central storage rooms to point of use instruments.

Modern analytical instruments such as gas chromatographs and mass spectrometers require uninterrupted, contamination free gas streams to produce accurate and repeatable results. Traditional cylinder setups located directly inside work areas create safety risks, consume valuable floor space, and introduce pressure fluctuations during manual tank replacements. LGS Lab Gas System eliminates these operational challenges by moving gas sources into dedicated exterior or isolated rooms and delivering media through continuous, orbital welded stainless steel pipelines.

The company portfolio covers every critical stage of gas management. At the source level, LGS provides fully automatic and semi automatic specialty gas cabinets, including the JW 300 GC and JW 200 GC models. Built with exhausted, explosion proof enclosures, programmable logic controller purge sequences, and ten inch touchscreens, these cabinets safely manage hazardous, toxic, and corrosive media such as silane, ammonia, hydrogen chloride, and nitrogen trifluoride. Automatic changeover manifolds monitor cylinder pressure in real time and switch seamlessly between primary and reserve banks without interrupting downstream operations.

For distribution and final delivery, LGS manufactures electropolished 316L and VIM VAR stainless steel tubing, valve manifold boxes, packless metal diaphragm valves, ultra high purity pressure regulators, and point of use outlet panels. Every wetted component undergoes strict surface finishing and cleaning to prevent outgassing, particle generation, and moisture ingress. Integrated gas leak detectors, excess flow switches, and emergency shutoff valves work together to protect personnel and facility assets around the clock.

Beyond component manufacturing, LGS Lab Gas System delivers complete turnkey engineering services. Experienced project teams support clients from initial site assessment and pipeline layout design through clean room assembly, automated orbital welding, helium leak testing, and final certification documentation. By combining matched hardware with certified installation practices, LGS helps laboratories achieve compliance with international safety codes while lowering long term maintenance costs.

About LGS Lab Gas System

Headquartered in Songjiang District, Shanghai, LGS Lab Gas System specializes in the design, production, and installation of ultra high purity laboratory gas systems and specialty gas equipment. Serving research institutions, universities, semiconductor plants, and life science laboratories worldwide, the company is dedicated to advancing laboratory safety, gas purity, and operational reliability.

data.title: Hyster-Yale Prices Upsized $135 Million Convertible Senior Notes Offering
data.description:
Hyster-Yale Prices Upsized $135 Million Convertible Senior Notes Offering

Hyster-Yale Prices Upsized $135 Million Convertible Senior Notes Offering

PR Newswire

CLEVELAND, Nov. 18, 2026

CLEVELAND, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyster‑Yale, Inc. (NYSE: HY) today announced the pricing of its offering of $135,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 7.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031 (the "notes") in a private offering to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"). The offering size was increased from the previously announced offering size of $125,000,000 aggregate principal amount of notes. The issuance and sale of the notes is scheduled to close on November 23, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Hyster‑Yale granted the initial purchasers of the notes an option to purchase, for settlement within a period of 13 days from, and including, the date the notes are first issued, up to an additional $20,000,000 aggregate principal amount of notes.

The notes will be general senior unsecured obligations of Hyster‑Yale and will accrue interest at a rate of 7.50% per annum, payable semi-annually in arrears on May 15 and November 15 of each year, beginning on May 15, 2027. The notes will mature on November 15, 2031, unless earlier repurchased, redeemed or converted in accordance with their terms. Before July 15, 2031, noteholders will have the right to convert their notes only upon the occurrence of certain events. At any time from, and including, July 15, 2031, noteholders may convert their notes at their election until the close of business on the second scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date, irrespective of these conditions. Hyster‑Yale will settle conversions by paying cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted and paying or delivering, as applicable, cash, shares of its Class A common stock (the "Class A common stock") or a combination of cash and shares of Class A common stock, at Hyster‑Yale's election, in respect of the remainder, if any, of its conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted. The initial conversion rate is 55.1207 shares of Class A common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes, which represents an initial conversion price of approximately $18.14 per share of Class A common stock. The initial conversion price represents a premium of approximately 17.5% over the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on November 18, 2026, which was $15.44 per share. The conversion rate will be subject to adjustment upon the occurrence of certain events, but will not be adjusted for any accrued and unpaid interest.

Hyster‑Yale may not redeem the notes prior to November 20, 2029, except in the event of a cleanup redemption (as defined below). The notes will be redeemable, in whole or in part (subject to certain limitations, including a partial redemption limitation), for cash at Hyster‑Yale's option at any time, and from time to time, on a redemption date on or after November 20, 2029 and before the 61st scheduled trading day immediately prior to the maturity date, if the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock has been at least 130% of the conversion price then in effect for a specified period of time and if certain other conditions are satisfied. The redemption price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the relevant redemption date.

In addition, Hyster‑Yale may redeem for cash all, but not less than all, of the notes at any time before the 61st scheduled trading day immediately prior to the maturity date if the aggregate principal amount of the notes that remains outstanding at such time is less than 10% of the aggregate principal amount of the notes initially issued under the indenture and certain other conditions are satisfied (a "cleanup redemption"). The redemption price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the relevant redemption date.

If certain corporate events that constitute a "fundamental change" (as defined in the indenture that will govern the notes) occur, then, subject to certain conditions and exceptions, noteholders may require Hyster‑Yale to repurchase their notes for cash. The fundamental change repurchase price will be equal to 100% of the principal amount of the notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the applicable fundamental change repurchase date.

Hyster‑Yale estimates that the net proceeds from the offering will be approximately $129.7 million (or approximately $149.1 million if the initial purchasers fully exercise their option to purchase additional notes), after deducting the initial purchasers' discounts and commissions and Hyster‑Yale's estimated offering expenses. Hyster‑Yale intends to use the net proceeds from the offering of the notes, together with cash on hand, (i) to repay $110.0 million of the $213.2 million principal amount outstanding under the term loan under its Amended and Restated Term Loan Credit Agreement, dated as of May 28, 2021 (the "2021 Credit Agreement"), (ii) to pay the approximately $13.5 million cost of the capped call transactions (as described below), (iii) to repurchase approximately $15 million of shares of Class A common stock concurrently with the pricing of the notes (as described below), and (iv) for general corporate purposes. If the initial purchasers exercise their option to purchase additional notes, Hyster‑Yale expects to use a portion of the net proceeds from the sale of the additional notes to enter into additional capped call transactions with the option counterparties, to repay additional principal amounts outstanding under the term loan under its 2021 Credit Agreement and, to the extent any proceeds remain, for general corporate purposes. The Company intends to repay the remaining principal amount outstanding under the term loan under its 2021 Credit Agreement on or prior to its maturity with additional long-term debt that is on terms acceptable to the Company.

Hyster‑Yale expects to use approximately $15 million of the net proceeds from the offering to repurchase approximately 971,000 shares of Class A common stock in privately negotiated transactions effected with or through one of the initial purchasers or its affiliate concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the notes (the "concurrent share repurchase"). The purchase price per share in the concurrent share repurchase will be $15.44 per share, which is the last reported sale price per share of Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on the date of the pricing of the notes. The concurrent share repurchase could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of Class A common stock, including concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the notes, and could have resulted in a higher effective conversion price for the notes. Hyster‑Yale cannot predict the magnitude of such market activity or the overall effect it will have on the price of the notes or the Class A common stock and the corresponding effect on the initial conversion price of the notes.

In connection with the pricing of the notes, Hyster‑Yale entered into privately negotiated capped call transactions with certain of the initial purchasers and their affiliates and certain other financial institutions (the "option counterparties"). The capped call transactions cover, subject to customary adjustments substantially similar to those applicable to the notes, the number of shares of Class A common stock initially underlying the notes. The capped call transactions are generally expected to reduce the potential dilution to the Class A common stock upon any conversion of the notes and/or offset any potential cash payments Hyster‑Yale is required to make in excess of the principal amount of such converted notes, as the case may be, with such reduction and/or offset subject to a cap based on the cap price. The cap price of the capped call transactions is initially $27.02 per share, which represents a premium of 75% over the last reported sale price per share of the Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on November 18, 2026 (which was $15.44 per share), and is subject to certain adjustments under the terms of the capped call transactions. If the initial purchasers exercise their option to purchase additional notes, then Hyster‑Yale expects to enter into additional capped call transactions with the option counterparties.

Hyster‑Yale has been advised that, in connection with establishing their initial hedges of the capped call transactions, the option counterparties or their respective affiliates expect to enter into various derivative transactions with respect to the Class A common stock and/or purchase shares of Class A common stock concurrently with, or shortly after, the pricing of the notes. This activity could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of the Class A common stock or the notes at that time.

In addition, Hyster-Yale has been advised that the option counterparties or their respective affiliates may modify their hedge positions by entering into or unwinding various derivatives with respect to the Class A common stock and/or purchasing or selling the Class A common stock or other securities of Hyster‑Yale in secondary market transactions following the pricing of the notes and prior to the maturity of the notes (and are likely to do so during any observation period related to a conversion of the notes, following any redemption of the notes or any repurchase of the notes upon a fundamental change, or, to the extent Hyster‑Yale exercises the relevant election under the capped call transactions, following any other repurchase of the notes). This activity could also cause or avoid an increase or a decrease in the market price of the Class A common stock or the notes, which could affect the ability of noteholders to convert the notes and, to the extent the activity occurs during any observation period related to a conversion of the notes, it could affect the number of shares of Class A common stock, if any, and value of the consideration that noteholders will receive upon conversion of the notes.

The notes are being offered only to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act. The offer and sale of the notes and any shares of Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of the notes have not been, and will not be, registered under the Securities Act or any other securities laws, and the notes and any such shares cannot be offered or sold except pursuant to an exemption from, or in a transaction not subject to, the registration requirements of the Securities Act and any other applicable securities laws. This press release does not constitute an offer to sell, or the solicitation of an offer to buy, the notes or any shares of Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of the notes, nor will there be any sale of the notes or any such shares, in any state or other jurisdiction in which such offer, sale or solicitation would be unlawful. This press release does not constitute an offer to buy any shares of Class A common stock in the contemplated repurchase.

Forward-looking Statements Disclaimer

The statements contained in this news release that are not historical facts are "forward-looking statements", including the statements regarding the notes being offered, the capped call transactions and the concurrent share repurchase, the completion of the proposed offering, the capped call and the concurrent share repurchase, the intended use of proceeds and the potential effects of the concurrent share repurchase. These forward-looking statements are made subject to certain risks and uncertainties, which could cause actual results to differ materially from those presented. Readers are cautioned not to place undue reliance on these forward-looking statements, which speak only as of the date hereof. The Company undertakes no obligation to publicly revise these forward-looking statements to reflect events or circumstances that arise after the date hereof. Among the factors that could cause plans, actions and results to differ materially from current expectations are, without limitation: (1) delays in delivery and other supply chain disruptions, or increases in costs as a result of inflation or otherwise, including materials, critical components and transportation costs and shortages, the effects of tariffs on raw materials or sourced products, and labor, or changes in or unavailability of quality suppliers or transporters, including the impacts of the foregoing risks on the Company's liquidity, (2) impacts resulting from current or changes in trade barriers and restrictions on international trade, including as a result of previously announced, and potentially new changes, including reductions to U.S. trade policy and tariffs as well as retaliatory or other tariffs imposed by other countries where the Company does business, (3) the effectiveness of the cost reduction programs implemented, and to be implemented globally, including the and related parts and service on a global basis, including any cyclical reduction in demand in the lift truck industry, (6) customer acceptance of pricing, (7) customer acceptance of, changes in the including without limitation the entry into new trade agreements and the imposition of tariffs and/or economic sanctions, including the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, which could impact Hyster‑Yale's imports from China, as well as armed conflicts, including the Iran conflict, the Russia/Ukraine conflict, the Israel and Gaza conflict and/or the conflict in the Red Sea, and their countries, (14) bankruptcy of or loss of major dealers, retail customers or suppliers, (15) introduction of new products by, more favorable product pricing offered by or shorter lead times available through competitors, (16) product liability or other litigation, warranty claims or returns of products, (17) changes mandated by federal, state and other regulation, including tax, health, safety or breaches.

Hyster‑Yale may not consummate the proposed offering described in this news release and, if the proposed offering is consummated, cannot provide any assurances regarding its ability to effectively apply the net proceeds as described above. Readers should understand that it is not possible to predict or identify all such factors and, consequently, should not consider any such list to be a complete set of all potential risks or uncertainties.

About Hyster‑Yale, Inc.

Hyster‑Yale, Inc., headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, is a globally integrated company offering a full line of lift trucks and solutions, including attachments aimed at meeting the specific materials handling needs of its customers. Hyster‑Yale's vision is to transform the way the world moves materials from Port to Home and deliver on its customer promises of: (1) thoroughly understanding customer applications and offering optimal solutions that will improve productivity at the lowest cost of ownership, and (2) providing exceptional customer care to create increasing value from initial engagement through the product lifecycle.

data.title: JOYY Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results: Total revenues record consistent increases, driven by sustained growth of three core businesses
data.description:
JOYY Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results: Total revenues record consistent increases, driven by sustained growth of three core businesses

JOYY Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results: Total revenues record consistent increases, driven by sustained growth of three core businesses

PR Newswire

SINGAPORE, Nov. 18, 2026

SINGAPORE, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- JOYY Inc. (NASDAQ: JOYY) ("JOYY" or the "Company"), a leading global technology company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

In the third quarter, JOYY maintained solid growth momentum. Total revenues reached US$624.6 million, up 15.6% year over year and 5.7% quarter over quarter. Social entertainment revenue was US$441.0 million, up 8.8% year over year. BIGO Ads, including both first-party and third-party businesses, generated US$145.7 million in revenue, up 39.6% year over year, with its third-party advertising business sustaining strong growth of 52.3% year over year. SHOPLINE revenue reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year. The contribution from non-livestreaming revenue further increased to 32.8% of total revenues this quarter, driven by the Company's multi-engine growth strategy.

JOYY's non-GAAP operating income reached US$46.6 million, up 14.6% year over year. Non-GAAP EBITDA reached US$55.7 million, up 10.1% year over year. Operating cash inflow for the quarter was US$102.2 million. As of September 30, 2026, JOYY held US$2.94 billion in net cash. Supported by the Company's strong cash flow generation and solid financial position, it continued to return capital to its shareholders for their long-term support through cash dividends and share repurchases. As of November 13, the Company has returned a total of US$536.0 million to shareholders this year.

Ms. Ting Li, Chairperson and Chief Executive Officer of JOYY, commented, "We have continued to execute our multi-engine growth strategy, strengthening our core Social Entertainment business while developing Ad Tech and Smart Commerce as two new growth engines. Following our investments and business model validation over the past few years, the results of this strategy are becoming increasingly evident in sustained topline expansion. Looking ahead to 2027, we believe JOYY will enter an important phase as we advance our multi-engine growth strategy and translate our progress into stronger operating results. With increasingly clear growth paths across our three businesses, we are confident in the Company's ability to sustain solid revenue growth in 2027. We also expect greater scale, a stronger earnings mix, and improved operating efficiency to drive further growth in operating profitability." 

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Net revenues in the third quarter of 2026 were US$624.6 million, representing an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    - Social Entertainment revenue was US$441.0 million, representing an increase of 8.8% from US$405.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    - BIGO Ads revenue was US$145.7 million, representing an increase of 39.6% from US$104.4 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    - SHOPLINE revenue was US$37.8 million, representing an increase of 24.7% from US$30.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Operating income was US$13.5 million.
  • Non-GAAP1 operating income was US$46.6 million, representing an increase of 14.6% from US$40.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Non-GAAP1 EBITDA was US$55.7 million, representing an increase of 10.1% from US$50.6 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net cash as of September 30, 2026 was US$2940.5 million.
  • Net cash from operating activities was US$102.2 million.

Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights

Social Entertainment Business

In the third quarter, Social Entertainment continued to deliver steady growth, with year-over-year growth momentum further accelerating. The Company's global average mobile MAUs reached 278.8 million, up 4.7% year over year. Livestreaming revenue reached US$419.8 million, up 8.1% year over year and 4.3% quarter over quarter. Driven by effective and refined operations, the number of core livestreaming paying users grew 8.1% year over year and 4.8% quarter over quarter.

Bigo Live, the Company's flagship product, continued its steady revenue growth, supported by ongoing improvements in content operations, its streamer ecosystem, and AI applications. In content operations, Bigo Live continued to build on its strengths as a global social platform to better cater to users' cross-regional content consumption and social interaction needs. Bigo Live further refined its cross-regional content distribution algorithms, expanded live translation coverage, and enhanced speech recognition in complex acoustic environments, making it easier for cross-language communication. These improvements drove continued growth in cross-regional gifting among users in developed markets. In terms of the streamer ecosystem, Bigo Live continued to invest in its community by refining growth and incentive mechanisms for new streamers. In particular, Bigo Live improved onboarding and guidance to help newly signed streamers successfully launch their first livestreams. These efforts contributed to a 4.7-percentage-point increase in the share of newly signed streamers completing their first livestream compared with the previous quarter, bolstering Bigo Live's high-quality content pipeline. Bigo Live continued to integrate AI into livestream interactions and virtual gifting, expanding its AI-generated interactive content and virtual gifts to create a more personalized experience for users. In September, the share of total virtual gift consumption attributable to AI-generated interactive virtual gifts increased further to 35.4%.

Furthermore, Bigo Live continued to deepen local community engagement and foster vibrant creator ecosystems. In the Middle East and North Africa, as an official content partner of the 2026 Esports World Cup, Bigo Live delivered an immersive viewing format that integrated tournament livestreams with interactive experiences. Across Southeast Asia, Bigo Live hosted multiple mid-year galas in local markets, supporting the growth of local creators and the sustainable development of its ecosystem. In North America, BIGO Academy combined online growth challenges with offline recognition, highlighting the vitality of its creator ecosystem and strong user engagement. In South America, Bigo Live held its inaugural offline event in Brazil and organized roadshows in Colombia and Peru, expanding public awareness of the platform and fostering a more vibrant and inclusive local creator ecosystem.

BIGO Ads Advertising Technology Business

In the third quarter, BIGO Ads continued to expand its global traffic network, diversify its advertiser verticals and demand mix, while improving its algorithms and ad delivery efficiency. As a result, BIGO Ads' revenue reached US$145.7 million, up 39.6% year over year and 9.0% quarter over quarter. Its third-party advertising business, BIGO Audience Network, grew 52.3% year over year and 9.2% quarter over quarter.

On the supply side, BIGO Ads continued to expand its global developer ecosystem and broaden the high-quality traffic coverage. In the third quarter, SDK traffic grew 55.6% year over year. In October, BIGO Ads SDK became generally available via Google AdMob™ Mediation as an in-app bidding partner. Developers can now seamlessly access the BIGO Ads SDK through Google AdMob Mediation and tap into massive demand from global premium advertisers. This integration creates new opportunities for BIGO Ads to expand its premium traffic supply and reach a broader range of app categories.

On the demand side, BIGO Ads continued to strengthen its presence in key verticals by expanding its local advertiser base and accumulating more advertiser conversion data. These insights helped further refine its algorithms and optimize ad delivery solutions across different web-based verticals. Web-based advertising demand continued to accelerate, growing by approximately 328% year over year and 30% quarter over quarter, becoming a key driver of BIGO Ads' growth this quarter. Meanwhile, in-app demand maintained healthy growth momentum.

On the technology side, BIGO Ads continued to enhance its data and AI-driven algorithm capabilities to improve the precision and efficiency of ad delivery. As its cross-channel attribution systems improved and advertiser conversion data accumulated, the platform further upgraded its model architecture to support multiple conversion objectives and types of traffic, improving algorithm accuracy and iteration efficiency. Meanwhile, BIGO Ads continued to refine its bidding strategies to better assess the value of each ad impression and match advertiser budgets with available inventory more effectively. These improvements helped advertisers meet their ROI targets while enhancing the efficiency of BIGO Ads' traffic acquisition and monetization.

SHOPLINE E-Commerce Business

In the third quarter, SHOPLINE continued to focus on acquiring high-quality brand merchants, strengthening its presence in key markets, and enhancing its omnichannel commerce infrastructure and value-added services. SHOPLINE's revenue reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year and 10.0% quarter over quarter.

In the cross-border business, SHOPLINE enhanced its service offerings and local support to help these merchants migrate to its platform, manage operations across markets, and process cross-border transactions more efficiently. In the third quarter, revenue from cross-border merchants maintained strong momentum, growing 77.8% year over year. To support the growing base of brand merchants, the Company continued to enhance SHOPLINE Payments with more local payment options, stronger multi-currency payment support, and improved transaction management. These enhancements helped merchants manage cross-border payments easily and efficiently.

In AI Commerce, SHOPLINE's strategy revolves around helping merchants capture demand from AI channels and improve their operational efficiency. As AI agents change how consumers discover and purchase products, SHOPLINE continued to strengthen its capabilities and expand integrations with the broader AI ecosystem. While volume from AI channels is still in an early stage, adoption is building quickly. In the third quarter, page views and order volume from AI channels grew nearly 500% and 550% year over year, respectively. Notably, AI is demonstrating distinct advantages in categories such as consumer electronics and furniture, where shoppers weigh multiple options before buying. In these categories, AI can better interpret consumer needs, recommend relevant products, and guide shoppers toward a purchase. SHOPLINE Omi, an AI-powered commerce assistant, has rolled out features spanning product management, customer segmentation, promotional events, guidance on platform features and settings, and detailed store performance analysis, bringing AI deeper into merchants' day-to-day workflows and improving operational efficiency.

  1. The non-GAAP financial measures provided above should not be considered as a substitute for, or superior to, the measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP. For details of the non-GAAP measures, including the reconciliations of GAAP measures to non-GAAP measures, please refer to the press release titled "JOYY Reports Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results" issued by the Company on November 19, 2026.
  2. Google AdMob is a trademark or registered trademark of Google LLC.

data.title: From 2 to 8 Hours: HiTHIUM Showcases Full-Duration Portfolio and Sodium-Ion Solution at RE+ 2026
data.description:
From 2 to 8 Hours: HiTHIUM Showcases Full-Duration Portfolio and Sodium-Ion Solution at RE+ 2026

From 2 to 8 Hours: HiTHIUM Showcases Full-Duration Portfolio and Sodium-Ion Solution at RE+ 2026

PR Newswire

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 18, 2026

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- From November 17 to 19, 2026, HiTHIUM, a leading global energy storage technology company, showcased its integrated energy storage solutions and end-to-end delivery capabilities at RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas. Organized around storage duration, the exhibition featured solutions spanning 2 to 8 hours, highlighting HiTHIUM's lithium-sodium technology portfolio, grid integration capabilities, and applications for AI data centers and microgrids.

8-Hour LDES: Unlocking Greater Lifecycle Value

As renewable energy penetration increases across the United States, the duck curve is becoming more pronounced, particularly in solar-intensive markets such as California. Meanwhile, the rapid expansion of AI data centers and extreme weather events are driving greater demand for continuous power and grid resilience. These trends are strengthening the need for long-duration energy storage.

In response, HiTHIUM presented its ∞Power 6.9+MWh 8h solution, featuring a native 8-hour architecture in a standard 20-foot container and powered by its self-developed ∞Cell 1300+Ah battery cell. Designed for a 25-year service life, the system achieves a DC round-trip efficiency of at least 96%. Compared with a 5MWh configuration, it requires approximately one-quarter as many battery cells per GWh, 27% fewer containers, and 68% less peak auxiliary power, helping improve overall project economics.

Sodium-Ion Solutions: Broadening Technology Choices and Advancing Cost Competitiveness

Lithium resource concentration and price volatility are important considerations for U.S. customers. Sodium resources are more than 400 times as abundant as lithium and are more evenly distributed. As sodium-ion production scales, its cost is expected to decline toward parity with lithium-ion, expanding customers' technology choices.

HiTHIUM showcased its Next-Generation Sodium-Ion Energy Storage Solution ∞Power N4.0MWh, powered by its self-developed ∞Cell N785Ah sodium-ion battery cells. Designed for long-life energy storage applications, the solution features a cell cycle life of up to 20,000 cycles and a system design service life of 30 years. By advancing both lithium-ion and sodium-ion technologies, HiTHIUM is further expanding its energy storage technology portfolio and offering customers more options for diverse application scenarios.

Grid Integration: Strengthening Local Validation Capabilities

HiTHIUM also highlighted grid analysis and validation capabilities, including plant-level modelling, automated simulation, RMS and EMT benchmarking, hardware-in-the-loop verification and site measurement validation. Its SIT test platforms operate in Xiamen, Chongqing and Dallas; a European regional pre-commissioning platform is under construction in Spain and scheduled for completion in 2027.

Expanding into AIDC and Microgrid Applications

For AI data centers, HiTHIUM presented an integrated solution spanning battery containers, PCS, PPC, EMS and lifecycle services. Its portfolio includes LFP systems for durations above 2, 4 and 8 hours, as well as a sodium-ion option for durations above 2 hours.

For cold-chain warehousing, food processing and industrial parks, HiTHIUM's ∞Power 1022kWh liquid-cooled storage cabinet—integrated with PCS, on/off-grid switching and EMS—enables PV-storage coordination and critical-load backup. It stores surplus solar or off-peak power and discharges at peak to cut costs; during outages, it switches off-grid to prioritize refrigeration and other critical loads while dynamically managing remaining loads such as EV charging.

With integrated capabilities spanning product development, grid validation, and project delivery, HiTHIUM is committed to addressing the evolving needs of the North American market. Moving forward, the company will continue strengthening its local capabilities and delivering reliable, integrated energy storage solutions to support the region's energy transition.

data.title: 'I've been a stay-at-home mom': I'm 50 and have a chronic illness. My husband lost his job. Should he raid his 401(k)?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'Our financial and healthcare situation has become increasingly concerning'

"COBRA is too expensive. I also looked into Priority Health coverage and was quoted $1,400 per month, which is beyond what we can manage financially." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I am 50, and my husband recently lost his job. I have been a stay-at-home mom for many years and also live with a chronic illness that limits my ability to work full-time. I recently started working as a daycare aide at our local public school, but our financial and healthcare situation has become increasingly concerning.

I have several questions:

1. Health insurance and access to medical care

Unfortunately, my husband was not transparent with me about the circumstances surrounding his employment, so I wasn't given the opportunity to plan ahead for my healthcare needs. My health insurance was tied to his employment and, as a result, I was unable to renew my specialty medications or schedule an appointment with my neurologist.

COBRA is too expensive. I also looked into Priority Health coverage and was quoted $1,400 per month, which is beyond what we can manage. What other options should I explore? Are there affordable health insurance alternatives, marketplace plans, or assistance programs that could help someone in my situation?

2. My husband's 401(k) and retirement savings

My husband is considering withdrawing money from his 401(k). These funds are intended to support us during retirement. What is the best way to handle his 401(k)? Would rolling it over into an IRA or another retirement account be a better option than withdrawing the money? Are there ways to transfer or invest these funds without triggering unnecessary taxes?

3. My personal savings and retirement planning

I have $150,000 in a money-market account earning 3.1% interest. This money represents savings from my previous employment, along with funds I consistently set aside from our monthly household budget over the years. I want to make sure I am being responsible with this money and putting it to work for my future.

What would be the best way to manage these savings for retirement? Should I keep the money in a money-market account, consider CDs or high-yield savings accounts, or explore other investment options that could provide better long-term growth while protecting my principal? I need to make informed decisions and protect my financial future.

Feeling Insecure

Related: 'I have no financial safety net': I'm 66, rely on Social Security and have just $500 in savings. What hope do I have?

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually. Check out The Moneyist's private Facebook group.

He can apply for insurance outside the normal open-enrollment period from Nov. 1, 2026, through Jan. 15, 2027, on the ACA Marketplace.

Dear Insecure,

Your healthcare plan is an immediate priority, so sort that out ASAP.

Losing workplace health insurance qualifies your husband for a special enrollment period on healthcare.gov. He has a 60-day window after the loss of his coverage to pick a plan. The ACA Marketplace may ask for documents, including an employer or insurer notice, to verify when his coverage ends. The ACA Marketplace calculates his premium based on his age, location, household size and expected household income for the entire calendar year.

Importantly, he can apply outside the normal open-enrollment period, which runs from Nov. 1, 2026, through Jan. 15, 2027, on the ACA Marketplace. He may also qualify for an ACA subsidy. If he was earning $45,000 before being laid off and, assuming he doesn't have another job to go to, he will earn less for the remainder of the year; he will need to estimate his total income for 2026, which includes his salary up until the time he was laid off and unemployment benefits.

There is no asset test for most adults under 65 who qualify for the ACA Marketplace through the rules based on their modified adjusted gross income (MAGI). MAGI is calculated using adjusted gross income, taking certain adjustments or deductions into account. It's used to determine eligibility for certain tax deductions and credits, as well as certain government benefits and surcharges. The formula can change depending on what benefits you are applying for.

It's not so unusual to get sticker shock from COBRA's prices.

If your husband applies through the ACA Marketplace and his income appears low enough for Medicaid rather than Marketplace subsidies, the application should probably be referred to the relevant state program. Given that he has just lost his job and his income has dropped, tell him to check both state healthcare plans and ACA Marketplace plans. As you point out, it's not so unusual to get sticker shock from COBRA's prices.

COBRA can cost $800 a month for individual coverage and $2,300 for family coverage, depending on the plan. Again, he has 60 days to elect COBRA, and once he pays the required premiums, his coverage can be applied retroactively to when his employer coverage ended. To qualify for COBRA, the U.S. Labor Department says he must have been covered by his employer's group health plan, the plan must be subject to COBRA, and other qualifying conditions must be met.

Some Moneyist Facebook Group members weighed in on your questions. "Don't get distracted with things that don't matter," one wrote. "Rolling over your husband's 401(k) is not a priority. It can stay in his employer's custodian and roll over to a Schwab or Fidelity-type institution when things calm down. His focus needs to be 100% on getting a new job, not worrying about your retirement. You are nowhere near ready for retirement so employment is what matters."

Don't miss: 'It leaves me with a sour taste': My elderly mother gave our cousin $800 for a car repair. Should I be worried?

Retirement savings and planning

I understand why you and your husband might think withdrawing from your 401(k) could help, but it could have the opposite effect in the long run. I urge you to proceed cautiously. There's increasing evidence that, with the rising cost of living and stubbornly high interest rates, more Americans feel under pressure to dip into their retirement savings - sometimes as a short-term loan, which they may not be able to pay back.

If your husband does dip into his 401(k), he may be forced to pay a 10% penalty for withdrawing funds before 591/2 and, if that wasn't harsh enough, he will also be required to pay income tax on his early withdrawal. For example, if you need $50,000 to supplement your living expenses over the next 12 months, he may need to withdraw considerably more to account for taxes and potential penalties. The IRS has effectively made every effort to deter you from doing so.

There is a "rule of 55" for making unexpected or early withdrawals. If a person leaves or loses their job during or after the calendar year they turn 55, or age 50 for certain public-safety workers, they can make withdrawals from a 401(k) plan without having to pay that 10% penalty. Income taxes still apply, however, and the funds must remain in that employer's 401(k) rather than being rolled over to an IRA.

We are living in a "low fire, low hire" jobs environment.

Given your age, investing your $150,000 in a diversified stock-market portfolio could make more sense than a money-market account, high-yield savings account (HYSA) or CD. Keeping it in a money-market account (at a 3.1% interest rate) could give you around $203,500 over 10 years versus $222,000 in a HYSA or CD (at 4%), or $295,000 in a balanced portfolio (at 7%). The big caveat is that the stock market provides no guarantees.

There are no hard-and-fast rules, but many advisers recommend that someone around 50 consider an asset allocation of 60% to 80% equities and 20% to 40% fixed income (bonds and cash equivalents). However, your risk tolerance plays a big part in that. It would not be unusual to find someone who is invested in 90% or even, in some cases, 100% stocks at 50, given that they have another 15 years or more until they retire.

In the meantime, cut your costs and look into selling any valuables that could get you through this financial crunch. I trust your husband has applied for unemployment insurance and has pursued your health-insurance options before that 60-day window has closed. You will need patience. We are living in a "low fire, low hire" jobs environment. The average job search takes about three to six months, so be prepared for a hard slog.

Keep your cool and don't make any hasty decisions.

Related: My 93-year-old father changed his will at the 11th hour, leaving my brother his entire $500,000 estate. Can I challenge it?

data.title: Beyond Static Estimates: How Cisco's Product Carbon Footprint Feature Tracks a Decarbonizing Grid
data.description:
NORTHAMPTON, MA / ACCESS Newswire / November 18, 2026 / by Lucy Nguyen

Cisco

Businesses are setting ambitious net-zero targets while facing increasing demands for transparent, verifiable data on their Scope 3 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. For many, this is where the carbon footprint of purchased products, like Cisco hardware, can become a critical piece of the sustainability puzzle.

The challenge is getting data that is usable in real workflows: by product, by year, and at the scale required for procurement, reporting, and target tracking. To address this challenge, we evolved our product carbon footprint (PCF) data to not only estimate the GHG emissions of a product over its life cycle, but to incorporate the impact of growing electricity grid decarbonization over time.

Why static PCFs are evolving

Michael King, senior leader of carbon accounting and analytics at Cisco, recognized that a static carbon footprint number often misses the significant decarbonization efforts happening across the supply chain or the ongoing shift to cleaner energy grids.

"Companies ask for product carbon data they can use in their own accounting that's aligned to their base year, reporting year, and net-zero timeline," says King. So, he developed a robust methodology that goes beyond traditional static calculations to dynamically adjust PCFs, reflecting real-world decarbonization.

For example, a product purchased today will have a lower carbon footprint than the same product purchased five years ago, even if the physical product is identical, due to the cleaner electricity powering its production.

Here's how Cisco is approaching dynamic PCFs:

  • Identify hotspots: We start by pinpointing the components within Cisco products that contribute most significantly to GHG emissions. These "hotspots" can include printed circuit boards, integrated circuits, and the energy used in testing and assembly.
  • Isolate electricity emissions: For these hotspots, we determine the portion of emissions directly attributable to electricity consumption during manufacturing (representing Scope 2 emissions of our suppliers).
  • Adjust dynamically: We then leverage reputable global energy grid data and projections from organizations like the International Energy Agency (IEA). This allows us to:
    • Backcast: Recalculate historical PCFs, showing how a product's footprint would have looked in past years as grids were more carbon intensive.
    • Forecast: Project future PCFs, illustrating the anticipated reductions as energy grids continue to decarbonize based on forecasted scenarios.

From disclosure to decision-making

Dynamic PCF data offers a powerful advantage. It allows companies to:

  • Track progress: Measure the reduction in their Scope 3 emissions over time, directly linked to their procurement of Cisco products.
  • Set realistic targets: Use projections to inform net-zero pathways and demonstrate tangible progress to stakeholders and regulators.
  • Make informed decisions: Understand the benefits of upgrading to newer Cisco hardware, which often incorporates further design and manufacturing efficiencies.

Fraunhofer, a leading German research institute, has critically reviewed our static PCF methodology to facilitate alignment with international standards, like ISO 14067. We plan to have them review our dynamic PCF calculation as well, providing third-party validation that ensures the accuracy and reliability of our data.

Built to scale

We're operationalizing this data so partners and customers can access it in the tools and workflows they're already using.

  • For partners: PCF data is available through Cisco's price list API for eligible products. Reach out to your Partner Account Manager to learn more.
  • For customers: Cisco's Product Sustainability API provides direct access to PCF data, helping streamline reporting and meet specific decarbonization targets.
  • For industry collaboration: Cisco is exploring partnerships with third-party data aggregators to improve consistency of Cisco verified PCF data across the ecosystem.
